# Dorothy Pengelly

Oral history interviewee, aged 94 at the time of the interview, the daughter of a herring gutter who worked the season through the 1920s and 1930s. Introduced by [[ifeoma-clarke]] at the Merrin Maritime Collection, where Dorothy had been interviewed once before for the museum.

## The interview

- One interview on 2025-04-23, about an hour and fifty minutes, recorded with her written consent. Summary in [[dorothy-pengelly-interview-2025-04-23]]; method in [[run-an-oral-history-interview]].
- Consent terms in [[dorothy-pengelly-consent-form]]: background use for the novel, no direct quotation in the book without asking her again, her name only in the acknowledgements, and a copy of the recording for her and, at her choice, for the museum.
- The recording itself is a governed pointer, not transcribed in full: [[dorothy-pengelly-interview-recording]].

## What she gave the book

The rhythm and cost of the gutting work as her mother told it: the cut fingers bound in cotton strips, the speed, the singing, the crews of three, the way the season ruled the year. Almost none of it is a checkable fact, and that is how I treat it: as texture and as a test of whether the curing-yard chapters feel lived in. The open question of how far I may go is [[how-much-of-dorothys-story-can-the-novel-use]].

## Since

- Sent her a typed thank-you letter and the summary on 2025-05-02; she corrected two names of curing firms, which I then removed from my notes altogether because they were real.
- Christmas card 2025. Promised to send her a copy of the book when it is accepted.

## Boundaries

No personal details beyond what she chose to tell for the interview and agreed I could use. Her family, address and health are not recorded here.
